- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 68–70), model tends to hold or overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5 points.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0 to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7 to forecast if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is volatile, model overreacts; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
